subtype: Approach: working backward from a target role [Thinking]
passage:
I sit next to Devika, and last month I watched Devika try to plan the next five years. Devika wants to be a software architect before thirty. On a big sheet taped to the wall, in three columns, went what that job needs: designing whole systems, leading a team, and knowing one field really well.
Then came the years. Year one: system design, with a course and one design document a quarter. Year two: lead a small team on a project. Year three: go deep on one business area. Later years were pencilled in lightly.
Devika stepped back and said, "Okay." I couldn't tell if that meant excited or scared. Probably both.
— Swati

qa.q: What three things did Devika list as needed for the job?
qa.a: Devika listed designing whole systems, leading a team and knowing one field well.

qa.q: What might Devika have been feeling when stepping back from the sheet and saying "Okay"?
qa.a: Devika might have felt excited and scared at once, though Swati cannot tell which.

qa.q: What could Devika do if year one's course turns out weaker than expected?
qa.a: Devika could swap it for another way to learn design, such as a design review with a senior colleague, and keep the yearly slot.

qa.q: What is it like for Swati to watch Devika plan?
qa.a: Swati feels curious and a little impressed, and also uncertain about what Devika feels.

grounding: The account shows a developer aiming to become an architect who lists what the role needs and assigns each item to a year.

passage:
Sunday. Irawati, twenty-four, writes at the top of a notebook page: 'Architect by 29.' Madhav, her flatmate, asks what an architect actually does. 'That's the point,' she says. 'I don't know yet.'
Wednesday. After work she reads three job descriptions and asks the architect on her team, Mrs Kulkarni, for twenty minutes. She comes home with a list: system design, leading a small team, deep knowledge of one area, like payments.
The next Saturday. She draws five columns, one for each year. System design goes into years one and two: a course, then designing one real service. Leading goes into year three: mentor two juniors first. Payments depth, years three to five. Madhav looks at the page. 'So it's not a dream anymore. It's a schedule.'

qa.q: What did Irawati write at the top of the notebook page?
What does Irawati's answer 'I don't know yet' show about how she feels?
qa.a: It shows she is curious and honest about not knowing, eager to find out what the role really needs.

qa.q: What else could Irawati do to test the plan?
qa.a: She could go through the plan with Mrs Kulkarni each year and adjust it if the role or her interests change.

qa.q: How might Madhav see the plan by Saturday?
qa.a: Madhav sees a vague dream turned into a practical schedule, and seems impressed.

grounding: It shows a developer working backward from becoming an architect by twenty-nine, listing what the role needs and assigning each part to a year.

subtype: Approach: working backward from a target role [Thinking]
passage: Farida, you said you want to be a principal engineer 'someday'. When I was twenty-five, your Preeti ma'am said 'someday' too, and for two years nothing happened. Then my boss asked me, 'What does that job actually need?' I didn't know. So I went and asked three architects over lunch. They said the same things: designing systems, leading people, and knowing one business deeply. I went home and made a five-year page. Year one: design courses and one small design of my own. Year two: take over a module. Year three: lead two juniors. Years four and five: become the person everyone asks about logistics systems. I stuck it inside my cupboard door. At thirty, I got the title. Not because I was brilliant. Because 'someday' became year one, year two.

qa.q: Who did Preeti ask about what the job needed?
How did Preeti feel during the two years of 'someday'?
qa.a: She was probably frustrated and stuck, wanting the role but with nothing actually moving.

qa.q: What was the turning point in Preeti's story?
qa.a: Her boss's question about what the job needed, which led her to ask architects and work backward into a five-year page.

qa.q: How might Preeti's boss have seen the change after that question?
qa.a: The boss likely noticed her taking on design work and a module year by year, and felt the question had been worth asking.

grounding: It shows a young engineer working backward from a target role, listing what it needs and assigning each skill to a year.
